text: Long ago, a young man named Giovanni Guasconti left his home in the south of Italy and came to Padua to pursue his studies at its ancient and famous university. <break time="0.8s" /> Having only a few coins in his pocket, he took a high and gloomy chamber in an old mansion, which had once belonged to a noble family of Padua. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking down from his window, Giovanni saw a garden of rare plants, in whose center stood the ruin of a marble fountain that still sent up its sparkling water. <break time="0.8s" /> A soft gurgling rose to his window and made him feel as if the fountain were an immortal spirit, singing its song endlessly without heeding the changes around it. <break time="0.8s" /> Beside the fountain grew a shrub with purple blossoms, each of which had the luster of a gem, and the whole was so bright that it seemed able to illuminate the garden even had there been no sunshine. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon a tall, thin, sallow man in a scholars black gown came into the garden and examined each plant with a cold, intent gaze, as though reading its innermost secrets. <break time="0.8s" /> Though his hands were gloved, he avoided even their scent, and when he reached the purple shrub, he placed a mask over his mouth, as if its beauty concealed a deadly malice. <break time="0.8s" /> He called for his daughter Beatrice, a girl as radiant as the blossoms themselves, who bent over the shrub without fear, embraced it, and whispered, Yes, my sister, your breath is the breath of life to me.
